title: Computer Use: Claude, OpenAI CUA, Gemini

questions.question: What input does Claude computer use take, and what does it emit?
options: Accessibility tree in, keyboard/mouse commands out
DOM XML parsed from the live page in, raw JavaScript out
Screenshots in (vision-based), keyboard/mouse commands out
Structured JSON in, a generated SQL query against the page out
questions.explanation: Claude reads pixels and emits keyboard/mouse actions; no OS accessibility API is used.

questions.question: What is Gemini 2.5 Computer Use's distinguishing safety feature?
options: Hard-coded WAF rules that block a fixed list of known-bad domains only, always
Mandatory CAPTCHA challenges inserted before every sensitive action taken
A read-only mode that is the model's default operating configuration always
A per-step safety service that assesses each action before execution and rejects unsafe ones
questions.explanation: Gemini 2.5 Computer Use ships a per-step safety classifier as a defining feature.

questions.question: What does the lesson identify as untrusted input across all three models?
options: Screenshots, DOM text, tool outputs, PDF content, anything retrieved
Only responses received over a plain, unencrypted HTTP connection today
Only the raw text content extracted from a PDF attachment specifically
Nothing; every input source is treated as fully trusted by default
questions.explanation: Only direct user instructions count as permission; everything else is untrusted.

questions.question: Which OSWorld / WebArena numbers does the lesson cite for OpenAI CUA at launch?
options: OSWorld success rate of exactly 0%, WebArena also at exactly 0% flat rate
Launch numbers cited were OSWorld 38.1%, WebArena 58.1%, WebVoyager 87%
OSWorld success rate of 99%, WebArena success rate also at exactly 99%
The launch announcement did not report any benchmark numbers at all
questions.explanation: Those were the launch numbers cited.

questions.question: Which defense pattern is NOT in the 2026 convergence list?
options: A per-step safety classifier that reviews each action first
An allowlist/blocklist restricting which navigation targets are reachable
Auto-clicking through confirmation dialogs to save time on each run
Human-in-the-loop confirmation required for sensitive actions
questions.explanation: Auto-clicking dialogs is the opposite of safe; the lesson recommends explicit confirmation.

questions.question: What is the principal attack the lesson highlights against computer-use agents?
options: A transient network outage that drops the agent's connection mid-action sequence
Rendering that runs slowly enough to desync the screenshot stream from real state
OS update lag that silently changes menu layouts between successive benchmark runs
A malicious page or PDF embedding instructions in retrieved content that the model treats as user intent
questions.explanation: Trusting screenshots or DOM text as permission is the canonical indirect-prompt-injection failure.

questions.question: When is human-in-the-loop confirmation specifically recommended?
options: On sensitive actions like login, purchase, file delete
Only on navigation that is strictly read-only and changes nothing
Only whenever the model itself decides to ask for confirmation
Never; confirmation is not part of any of the three models' design
questions.explanation: Sensitive actions (money, data exposure, new logins) require explicit human confirmation.
